---
title: "JQIDistributionalAnalysis"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}

# ============================================================
# CONSTRUCT AUTHORITATIVE INDUSTRY-YEAR JQI
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(gssrdoc)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load industry-year component panel
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_jqi <- read_csv(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)

glimpse(industry_jqi)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Standardize the five underlying indicators
#
# Higher values always indicate better job quality:
#
# wage_premium             = higher is better
# wage_cost_per_hour       = higher is better
# benefits_nonrequired     = higher is better
# layoffs_discharge_rate   = LOWER is better -> reverse
# earnings_volatility      = LOWER is better -> reverse
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions <- industry_jqi %>%
  mutate(
    z_wage_premium =
      as.numeric(scale(wage_premium)),

    z_ecec_wage =
      as.numeric(scale(wage_cost_per_hour)),

    z_benefits =
      as.numeric(scale(benefits_nonrequired)),

    z_stability =
      as.numeric(scale(-layoffs_discharge_rate)),

    z_earnings_stability =
      as.numeric(scale(-earnings_volatility))
  ) %>%
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Construct four substantive dimensions
  #
  # Compensation = average of wage premium and ECEC wage
  # Benefits     = benefits
  # Stability    = employment stability
  # Earnings     = earnings stability
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  mutate(
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_ecec_wage
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),

    benefits = z_benefits,

    stability = z_stability,

    earnings_stability = z_earnings_stability
  ) %>%
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Equal-weight the four dimensions
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  mutate(
    jqi = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        compensation,
        benefits,
        stability,
        earnings_stability
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Standardize the composite across the external panel
  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  
  mutate(
    jqi_z = as.numeric(scale(jqi))
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Verify the JQI construction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    jqi_mean = mean(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_sd = sd(jqi, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_z_mean = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    jqi_z_sd = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Verify the expected complete-JQI coverage
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions %>%
  summarise(
    complete_jqi = sum(!is.na(jqi)),
    total = n()
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Check the industry-year structure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_dimensions %>%
  count(year, industry_common) %>%
  filter(n > 1)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Continuous JQI distribution by year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_jqi <- job_quality_dimensions

jqi_year_summary <- industry_jqi %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi_z)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n(),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_jqi = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_jqi = min(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    p25_jqi = quantile(jqi_z, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_jqi = median(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    p75_jqi = quantile(jqi_z, .75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_jqi = max(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(jqi_year_summary, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define "quality industry" within each year
#
# Top 25% of industries in that year.
# This is a relative measure: an industry can be a
# quality industry in one year and not another.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_jqi <- industry_jqi %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_year_quartile = ntile(jqi_z, 4),
    quality_industry = if_else(
      jqi_year_quartile == 4,
      1L,
      0L
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Which industries are "quality industries" over time?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

quality_industry_summary <- industry_jqi %>%
  filter(!is.na(jqi_z)) %>%
  group_by(industry_common) %>%
  summarise(
    years_observed = n(),
    years_quality = sum(
      quality_industry == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    pct_years_quality = 100 * mean(
      quality_industry == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_jqi))

print(quality_industry_summary, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Industry trajectories
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_trajectory <- ggplot(
  industry_jqi %>%
    filter(!is.na(jqi_z)),
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = jqi_z,
    group = industry_common
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = .6) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Objective job quality (JQI)",
    title = "Objective job quality across industries, 2000–2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "TrajectoryofJQI.png"),
  plot = industry_trajectory
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. JQI distribution by year
#
# This shows how much the cross-industry distribution shifts
# over time rather than only showing the mean.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqibyyear <- ggplot(
  industry_jqi %>%
    filter(!is.na(jqi_z)),
  aes(
    x = factor(year),
    y = jqi_z
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Objective job quality (JQI)",
    title = "Distribution of objective job quality across industries"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "JQIbyYear.png"),
  plot = jqibyyear
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Heatmap: industry × year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqiheatmap <- ggplot(
  industry_jqi %>%
    filter(!is.na(jqi_z)),
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = reorder(industry_common, jqi_z, FUN = mean),
    fill = jqi_z
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Industry",
    fill = "JQI",
    title = "Objective job quality across industries and over time"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "JQIHeatmap.png"),
  plot = jqiheatmap
)
# ============================================================
# PART II: ASSIGN JQI AND QUALITY-INDUSTRY STATUS TO GSS
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Start from the GSS JQI analysis dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_distribution <- gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  select(
    everything()
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    quality_industry = case_when(
      !is.na(jqi_z) &
        !is.na(year) &
        !is.na(industry_common) ~
        industry_jqi$quality_industry[
          match(
            paste(year, industry_common),
            paste(
              industry_jqi$year,
              industry_jqi$industry_common
            )
          )
        ],
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  )


# Check assignment
gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    jqi_available = sum(!is.na(jqi_z)),
    quality_industry_available =
      sum(!is.na(quality_industry)),
    quality_industry_n =
      sum(quality_industry == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Distribution of GSS respondents across quality industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_quality_by_year <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(quality_industry)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    quality_industry_n =
      sum(quality_industry == 1),
    pct_quality_industry =
      100 * mean(quality_industry == 1),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_jqi = median(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(gss_quality_by_year, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Plot proportion of GSS respondents in quality industries
# ------------------------------------------------------------

highjqidistribution <- ggplot(
  gss_quality_by_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = pct_quality_industry
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = gss_quality_by_year$year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Percent in top-quartile JQI industries",
    title = "Share of GSS respondents employed in relatively high-quality industries"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "QualityJQIIndex.png"),
  plot = highjqidistribution
)
# ============================================================
# PART III: RACE STRATIFICATION
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. First identify the race variable in the dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------

names(gss_jqi_distribution)[
  grepl(
    "race",
    names(gss_jqi_distribution),
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
]


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Inspect the candidate race variable
#

# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_distribution %>% count(racecen1, sort = TRUE)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Continuous JQI by race and year
#
# This is the primary racial-access analysis.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_race_year <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(jqi_z),
    !is.na(racecen1)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, racecen1) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_jqi = sd(jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ci_low = mean_jqi - 1.96 * se_jqi,
    ci_high = mean_jqi + 1.96 * se_jqi
  )

print(jqi_race_year, n = 100)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Plot mean JQI by race over time
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_race_by_year <- ggplot(
  jqi_race_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = mean_jqi,
    group = racecen1
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = ci_low,
      ymax = ci_high
    ),
    width = .15
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(jqi_race_year$year))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Mean objective job quality (JQI)",
    title = "Objective job quality by race over time"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "JQIRacebyYear.png"),
  plot = jqi_race_by_year
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Quality-industry access by race and year
# ------------------------------------------------------------

quality_race_year <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(quality_industry),
    !is.na(racecen1)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, racecen1) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    quality_industry_n =
      sum(quality_industry == 1),
    pct_quality_industry =
      100 * mean(quality_industry == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(quality_race_year, n = 100)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Plot quality-industry access by race
# ------------------------------------------------------------

qual_by_race <- ggplot(
  quality_race_year,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = pct_quality_industry,
    group = racecen1
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = sort(unique(quality_race_year$year))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Percent in top-quartile JQI industries",
    title = "Access to relatively high-quality industries by race"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "QualityJQIByRace.png"),
  plot = qual_by_race
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Black/non-Black difference in continuous JQI
#
# Once the race coding is confirmed, create the Black indicator.
# ------------------------------------------------------------

gss_jqi_distribution <- gss_jqi_distribution %>%
  mutate(
    black = case_when(
      racecen1 == 2 ~ 1,
      !is.na(racecen1) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. Year-adjusted racial difference in JQI
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_jqi_race_year_fe <- lm(
  jqi_z ~ black + factor(year),
  data = gss_jqi_distribution %>%
    filter(!is.na(black), !is.na(jqi_z))
)

summary(m_jqi_race_year_fe)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 19. Does the Black/non-Black JQI gap change over time?
# ------------------------------------------------------------

m_jqi_race_year_interaction <- lm(
  jqi_z ~ black * factor(year),
  data = gss_jqi_distribution %>%
    filter(!is.na(black), !is.na(jqi_z))
)

summary(m_jqi_race_year_interaction)

race_gap_plot <- as.data.frame(
  summary(
    race_year_contrasts,
    infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)
  )
)

ggplot(
  race_gap_plot,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = estimate
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    width = .15
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = race_gap_plot$year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Black − non-Black JQI difference",
    title = "Black–non-Black difference in objective job quality over time",
    subtitle = "Estimates from year-interacted model with 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
